newsitem.title: CHINA: China trade surplus seen $15 bln for 1996.
newsitem.headline: China trade surplus seen $15 bln for 1996.

text.p: China is seen registering a trade surplus of $15 billion in 1996, the China Daily newspaper said on Saturday.

Exports were seen at $151.5 billion for 1996, up two percent from last year, the newspaper quoted Huang Guohua, an official with the statistics department of the General Administration of Customs, as saying.
Imports for 1996 were seen hitting $136.5 billion, a rise of 3.5 percent from last year, Huang said.
The newspaper gave no further details.
China registered a trade surplus of about $14 billion in the first 11 months of 1996, according to the latest official figures.
Exports in January-November were $132.78 billion, up 0.9 percent compared with the same period a year ago, the figures show.
Imports during the period were $118.81 billion, up 4.5 percent year-on-year, they show.
